claims.explanation: TWS-119 is a GSK3 inhibitor that activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, and its selective killing pattern tracks with intact, active β-catenin signaling rather than with any single lineage. Lines with upstream Wnt pathway activation (APC/CTNNB1 mutation, RNF43 loss, or high β-catenin/Wnt target expression) are sensitized, while lines with PTEN loss/PI3K-AKT activation or mesenchymal/low-Wnt states are protected. The transcriptional signature (MYC, CCND1, FOSL1, DUSP6 down; XBP1, MUC1, FGFR4 up) is consistent with GSK3 inhibition collapsing β-catenin/AP-1-driven proliferation in Wnt-dependent tumors.

features.basis: Activating β-catenin mutation predicts Wnt-pathway dependence and GSK3-inhibitor sensitivity (LOVO, SNU719 context)
APC loss activates canonical Wnt/β-catenin, the pathway TWS-119 engages
High Wnt/β-catenin target-gene output marks tumors dependent on GSK3-regulated β-catenin
TWS-119 transcriptionally downregulates MYC; MYC-addicted lines are more vulnerable
GSK3 inhibition destabilizes cyclin D1; high CCND1 lines depend on this axis
RNF43 loss removes negative feedback on Wnt receptors, increasing β-catenin drive
TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, consistent with loss of a GSK3/p53-linked checkpoint
PTEN loss/PI3K-AKT activation is enriched in least-affected lines and can bypass GSK3 dependence
PIK3CA-mutant lines (BT474, SNU719, HT115) are among least affected, suggesting PI3K drive compensates
BRAF-mutant melanoma/CRC lines are over-represented among least-affected, indicating MAPK bypass
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650) are strongly killed, linking RTK-driven Wnt crosstalk
NFE2L2-mutant squamous/bladder lines appear in the sensitive set, possibly via redox-metabolic dependency
